core_obligations: Part (1): combine base change of the one step devissage at the point with the fact that the inverse image of a standard open under a morphism of affine schemes is again standard open (proof lines 991-996).

Part (2): using that the morphism Y -> S is smooth hence open, find a standard open neighbourhood S' of s inside the image of W; then the fibres of W over S' are nonempty open subschemes of the original fibres and remain geometrically irreducible; define Z' as the preimage of Y' = W over S' and, choosing a function on Z cutting out the standard open Z', lift it to a function h on X and take X' to be the principal open of h, which gives the required standard shrinking (proof lines 998-1010).

Part (3): shrink the given open U so that it becomes a standard open, use the finite fibration lemma to find a standard open neighbourhood W of y whose preimage under the projection lies inside the preimage of U, apply part (2) to obtain a standard shrinking with middle scheme W over the chosen base, and then replace X' by its intersection with U, which is still standard open because U is, without violating the conditions of a standard shrinking (proof lines 1012-1023).
proof_roadmap: Part (1) by base change and functoriality of standard opens (proof lines 991-996).
Part (2) by openness of the smooth morphism, geometric irreducibility of the fibres, and lifting the local equation along the closed immersion (proof lines 998-1010).
Part (3) by the finite fibration lemma and an intersection with the standard open U (proof lines 1012-1023).
difficulty_reason: The lemma is the one step shrinking statement: any standard open neighbourhood of the base, of the middle scheme of a one step devissage, or of the point in the source can be met by a standard shrinking (statement lines 969-989, tag 05HA). Part (1) is a base change argument, but parts (2) and (3) require real constructions: part (2) uses openness of the smooth morphism to choose a base inside the image of the given neighbourhood, keeps geometric irreducibility of the fibres, and lifts the local equation cutting out the preimage through the closed immersion; part (3) uses the finite fibration lemma to find a neighbourhood of the middle scheme whose preimage lies in a given open and then intersects. Those constructions are the substance, so the claim is H2.
